title: Bitcoin Just Crashed Below $60,000 and Lost Half Its Value Since October. Here Is What NRI Investors Should Do Now.
excerpt: The cryptocurrency hit its lowest since 2024 after Michael Saylor's Strategy sold bitcoin for the first time and SpaceX's mega-IPO pulled capital from speculative assets
body:
Bitcoin briefly dipped below $60,000 on Friday, hitting its lowest intraday level since October 2024 and recording its worst weekly performance since the FTX collapse in late 2022. The world's largest cryptocurrency has now lost more than half its value since reaching a record high above $125,000 last October.

## What Triggered the Crash

Three forces converged this week.

First, Strategy — the bitcoin accumulation firm founded by Michael Saylor — disclosed that it had sold a portion of its massive bitcoin holdings for the first time since 2022. The disposal was a modest $2.5 million against Strategy's $50 billion-plus bitcoin stockpile, but it mattered because Saylor had explicitly pledged he would never sell. His statement in 2022 was unambiguous: "Never. No. We're not sellers. We're only acquiring and holding." The reversal shattered a psychological floor.

Second, SpaceX's impending IPO is pulling capital out of every speculative asset class. The Elon Musk conglomerate is seeking to raise up to $86 billion at a nearly $1.8 trillion valuation — a sum that demands liquidity from somewhere. Analysts at RBC BlueBay Asset Management noted that bitcoin is suffering from a classic "flavour of the month" rotation, losing capital to the newer, shinier opportunity.

Third, Friday's stronger-than-expected US jobs report — 172,000 new positions versus the 80,000 Wall Street expected — raised the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike later this year. Higher interest rates make speculative, non-yielding assets like bitcoin less attractive relative to risk-free treasury bills currently paying above 4 per cent.

## The Derivatives Accelerant

The slide below $60,000 was not just fundamental. On the Deribit options exchange, more than $1.2 billion in notional open interest sat at the $60,000 strike price in put options. As bitcoin approached that level, market makers who were short these puts were forced to sell spot bitcoin or futures to hedge their exposure, a process called delta hedging.

This mechanical selling accelerated the decline, turning what might have been an orderly pullback into a cascade. Leveraged long positions — bullish bets made with borrowed money — were liquidated in billions of dollars across the week, each liquidation adding further downward pressure.

## What This Means for NRI Investors

The timing is particularly painful for Indian diaspora investors who entered the crypto market in late 2024 and early 2025. After Donald Trump's election in November 2024, bitcoin surged on expectations of a crypto-friendly regulatory environment, and many first-time buyers entered at prices between $80,000 and $120,000. Those investors are now sitting on losses of 25 to 50 per cent.

In India, the situation is compounded by the 30 per cent flat tax on crypto gains and the 1 per cent TDS on transactions, which make it expensive to rebalance or exit positions. NRIs who hold crypto through Indian exchanges face an additional layer of regulatory uncertainty as the RBI continues to express scepticism about digital assets.

For NRIs holding bitcoin in US-based accounts, the question is whether to hold, cut losses, or average down. The honest answer: this depends entirely on your time horizon and your overall portfolio allocation.

## The Bull Case Is Not Dead, But It Is Bruised

Bitcoin bulls point out that the cryptocurrency has survived similar drawdowns before — a 75 per cent drop in 2022, a 50 per cent drop in 2021, an 84 per cent crash in 2018 — and eventually recovered to new highs. The network's fundamentals, including hashrate and wallet adoption, remain strong. And the asset's finite supply of 21 million coins has not changed.

But the competitive landscape has shifted. AI stocks have delivered returns that make bitcoin look staid: Nvidia is up over 150 per cent in 2026, and the Nasdaq, until this week's pullback, was at record highs. The opportunity cost of holding bitcoin versus tech equities has never been more visible.

Gold, the asset bitcoin was supposed to complement or replace as a store of value, is roughly flat for the year at around $4,490 an ounce. The S&P 500 is up about 8 per cent. Bitcoin, at minus 30 per cent, is the clear underperformer.

## The Practical Takeaway

If crypto makes up more than 5 to 10 per cent of your portfolio, this is a moment to reassess. The case for bitcoin as a diversifier depends on it moving independently of other risk assets, but this week it fell alongside stocks, was pressured by the same rate-hike fears, and was hurt by the same capital rotation towards equities. That correlation undermines the diversification thesis.

If you remain a long-term bitcoin believer, dollar-cost averaging at these levels — rather than trying to time the bottom — remains the least regrettable strategy. But be honest about why you own it: as a speculative bet on adoption, not as a safe haven.

**Sources:** Wall Street Journal, Reuters, CNN Business, CoinDesk, Investopedia; Strategy Inc. corporate disclosures; Deribit options data; LSEG market data
